title: Restore Trust in Monetization, Fix Workout Friction, and Turn Polarizing Feedback into Product Levers
overview: US App Store reviews reveal two intertwined trust problems—opaque paywalls and surprise billing—that are magnified by a free-tier ad experience that can block or hijack workouts. At the same time, the same features (subscription value, ad-supported access, workout content) split users into passionate fans and vocal detractors. This plan prioritizes fixing the monetization trust gap first, then closes the content/personalization gaps that make the app feel generic or exclusionary, and finally ships the concrete opportunities users asked for.

findings.title: Formerly free workouts moved behind subscription and forced ads, with perceived value split
findings.summary: A large group of reviewers—including people who used the app for years—report that workouts, daily plans, and saved routines that used to be free now require a paid subscription or a forced 90-second ad. Some describe the change as a bait-and-switch or say the app is no longer free, while a smaller group of subscribers sees the price as fair, cheaper than a gym, and worth it. The same monetization change produces both churn and strong loyalty.

findings.title: Surprise charges, broken free-trial terms, and unreachable billing or account support
findings.summary: Multiple reviewers report being charged immediately or after canceling despite advertised free trials, choosing a monthly plan and being billed for a full year, or being unable to cancel and get a refund. Others describe support contacts being blocked as spam, unanswered emails, and lost access to paid accounts. These incidents make paid commitments feel risky and severely damage trust.

findings.title: Free-tier ads are aggressive, hard to dismiss, and can hijack or block workouts
findings.summary: Free users describe long 90-second to 3-minute ads before every workout, hidden close buttons that force restarting the ad or the whole app, and ads that sometimes redirect users to an external shopping website. These interruptions turn free workouts into a churn risk, though a few reviewers tolerate or even defend the ad-supported tier.

findings.title: Workout usability strengths: short, varied, guided, and beginner-friendly sessions build loyalty
findings.summary: Satisfied reviewers repeatedly praise short workouts that fit busy schedules, clear instructions and demonstrations, variety across durations and levels, and the ability to build a daily habit. Some also highlight no-floor options and at-home convenience. A small number of users note one friction point, such as the Daily 7 only resetting after 24 hours.

findings.title: Personalization and onboarding miss user needs: ignored avoidances, forced goals, and exclusionary content
findings.summary: Users report that selected injury or exercise-avoidance preferences are ignored, plan settings reset without notice, and onboarding forces a weight-loss goal even when users want flexibility or other outcomes. A pregnant user says prenatal workouts included unsafe stomach-laying moves, and one reviewer calls the onboarding imagery anti-fat and alienating. These issues make the experience feel generic or exclusionary rather than tailored.

evidenceExcerpts.excerpt: if i select to avoid knees why does it still have lots of squats and lunges
i have to keep resetting the plan settings because they keep changing or defaulting without notice
i didn’t feel anything on my stomach where i’m supposed to get abs
the questionnaire is the exact same from all the other workout apps that i’ve downloaded
i just wish there were more free courses, or the option to watch an add to use all of the courses that are premium
i would like a longer interval time

you can’t even log in and use the app without setting a weight loss goal! every single exercise comes with a note on how much weight you’ll lose. i understand it’s useful if you are trying to lose weight, but the app specifically asks what your goals are (disappointed to find out that increasing flexibility wasn’t an option
i really want my things be harder and some of the things that even if it’s up to all the way, it’s not that hard
i stated my abs and there are so many ab workouts in my plan.
asks what to avoid but still includes moves that aggravate that area.
the quiz you take at the beginning does not affect the exercises you get.
i am unable to find any way to turn off the stupid jumping.
force me to choose a goal of weight loss for a healthy bmi ???
tell me why their prenatal workouts/yoga have you laying on your stomach doing single leg raises or supermans
it gave me a quiz with a bunch of creepy ai generated women which was really weird
the onboarding process is shocking. i was expecting something supportive of women and empowering. this app blatantly targets insecurities.

uncertainties: The knee-avoidance and plan-reset complaints come from individual users and may be caused by settings use or app bugs that are not fully described.
Whether the abs workout targets the abs as promised is not objectively verified.
The weight-loss framing complaint and the difficulty-ceiling complaint are each from a single review, so this negative cluster is small.
We cannot verify whether this is a widespread personalization failure or confined to certain plans.
The no-jumping problem is described by only one reviewer, so its prevalence is unknown; the forced-weight-loss complaint may also reflect messaging rather than actual plan behavior.
The pregnancy safety complaint is a single detailed report and may not represent all prenatal programming.
This is a single reviewer's account and may not represent the broader user base.
limitations: Requests are scattered across different reviews, so the size of the affected audience is unknown.
Positive and negative reports may come from different app versions, and no demographic or usage data is available in excerpts.
One conflicting positive review says workouts target the areas you want, suggesting some users do see customization work as expected.
This finding combines two personalization complaints with one support complaint; no reviewer in the dataset confirms whether the premium settings behave differently.
Praise and criticism come from different users with different workout levels and goals.
No conflicting or corroborating onboarding reviews are present in this batch.

findings.title: Concrete opportunities: real-person demos, smartwatch sync, adaptive programs, and friction-reducing controls
findings.summary: Reviewers explicitly request features that are currently missing: real-people videos instead of illustrations for form guidance, Apple Watch compatibility for calorie burn, voice prompts that announce halfway and end-of-move cues, shorter ads, no-floor workouts, and programs for older adults with stiff joints. These are clear, actionable product openings.

evidenceExcerpts.excerpt: maybe add a strength training section in the app and maybe if this can sync with the apple watch that would be great too
the illustrated workout demos can be tough to follow to make sure your form is correct.
it’d be great if every workout had the verbal prompts to indicate when a move is half done and to count down to the end of the move.
it would be better if the ads were shorter though
i also appreciate that i can do a workout that doesn’t include floor exercises.
i wish someone would create a program for those of us who are older, much older with muscles that have contracted and joints that are stiff.
don’t ask for my input if you will not do anything about my suggestion which i submitted a long ago with absolutely no response from anyone!

uncertainties: Only one review explicitly requests smartwatch sync and strength training, so demand size is unknown.
Requests come from a small number of individual reviews; no evidence that these are top requests for all users.
Whether these requests reflect broad demand or a few individual preferences is unknown from this sample.
limitations: Small sample; cannot estimate how many users beyond these reviewers would value these features.
The app may already support some of these options in versions or settings not reflected in these reviews.
Each request is supported by a single review.

findings.title: Subscription pricing and value are sharply split: transformative for some, an overpriced paywall for others
findings.summary: Paying users describe the subscription as body-changing, motivating, and cheaper than a gym, while other users see the same price as unaffordable or an unjustified paywall for features that were once free. Perceived subscription value is deeply polarized, and billing frustrations amplify the negative side.

evidenceExcerpts.excerpt: completely transformed my body composition
they give you more bang for your buck especially in endurance and mobility
i exercise with way more variety and frequency because of it
this app has been a huge help keeping me focused and motivated to workout right from home
great app with easy to follow workouts
it charged my card $39.99 for a yearly subscription despite me cancelling
you can only use the app if you buy the subscription.
still making me pay when i canceled my subscription.
the app still took the money out, when i contacted support, the site said me asking to cancel and get a refund was a scam.
now it’s all behind a subscription.
i need to pay when it’s suppose to be free.
now of course there’s a subscription fee. ridiculous.
it’s no longer free to use

uncertainties: The positive subscription reviews do not state whether they are comparing to the current free tier; the negative ones often reference an older free experience.
Review text is self-reported; we cannot verify whether surprise charges are due to user error, trial terms, or app bugs.
limitations: Ratings alone do not reveal how long subscribers have been paying or whether the discounted annual deal is still available; price sensitivity varies heavily by individual.
The free-tier and subscription behavior described may reflect different app versions or time periods.

requirements.title: Make paywall boundaries explicit before users start a workout
requirements.description: Reviewers repeatedly discover that 'free' workouts are actually premium-only, that saved routines are locked after updates, and that a paywall appears only after they invest time in onboarding. Fix this by showing a persistent Free / Free with ads / Premium badge on all content and a pre-start modal with exact terms before any paywall is encountered.
acceptanceCriteria: All workout, routine, program, and collection tiles display a persistent badge of 'Free', 'Free with ads', or 'Premium' before the user taps to open or start; no tile may omit the badge.
A tile labeled 'Free' must allow the user to finish the workout without payment; if an ad is required, a pre-start notice says 'Watch a short ad to unlock this workout'.
A tile labeled 'Premium' must never display the word 'Free' in its title, subtitle, or call-to-action.

When a free-tier user attempts to start a Premium workout, a pre-start modal states the exact price and billing period, what is included, and the user's remaining free-trial/free-credit status; exiting the modal returns to the previous screen and does not auto-start a trial.

Onboarding, questionnaires, and goal-setting flows must show the free/paid content split before any final paywall; if the user abandons at the paywall, the data entered during onboarding must not be saved into an active paid plan.

planningFactors.rationale: Finding 1 shows this is a frequent reason for churn and trust loss; finding 8 highlights the same feature is praised by subscribers, so transparency is the bridge between the two sides. Scope is medium because it touches UI labels, content metadata, and onboarding flow.

requirements.title: Guarantee free-trial and billing integrity with visible subscription management
requirements.description: Multiple reviewers report being charged immediately during a free trial, being billed for a full year when they chose monthly, or being charged after canceling. They also cannot find subscription management in the app. Fix the purchase flow and make cancellation and billing status visible and controllable from the app.
acceptanceCriteria: Purchases during a 'free trial' must not charge any amount until the trial end date, unless the user explicitly confirms a paid plan during the trial with an additional confirmation step. Suggested: no charge at trial start.
The app's Settings/Account screen shows a 'Manage Subscription' item within two taps from the home screen, linking to the App Store subscription page or an in-app management screen.

Cancellation initiated from the App Store subscription page is reflected in the app immediately: the app no longer promotes premium-only content as available and shows a 'Premium expires on <date>' status.

If a user selects a monthly plan, the app must not bill them for an annual plan; the selected billing interval and charge amount must appear in the purchase confirmation and on the post-purchase receipt screen.
For auto-renewing subscriptions, a push/email reminder is sent at least 24 hours before the first charge and before each renewal (Suggested: 24 hours before renewal).

planningFactors.rationale: Finding 2 and several supporting reviews in finding 8 describe real money being taken without clear consent, which is the highest-severity trust issue. Scope is medium because it involves StoreKit purchase flows, subscription management UI, and notification scheduling.

requirements.title: Fix free-tier ad experience: bounded length, always-dismissable, no redirects
requirements.description: Free users report 90-second to 3-minute ads, hidden close buttons, ads that restart after closing, and auto-redirects to external shopping sites. These interruptions turn free workouts into a churn risk. Fix the ad SDK integration and enforce dismissability, duration limits, and no redirects.
acceptanceCriteria: No ad unit shown before a workout may exceed 90 seconds in duration (derived from the most commonly reported 90-second ad complaints; Suggested: target 30 seconds or less).

Every ad must display a visible close/skip control no later than 15 seconds into the ad or immediately when the ad's video content finishes, whichever comes first (Suggested: show the close control for the entire ad).
Tapping close returns the user to the workout start screen in under 1 second and does not restart the same ad or enqueue another ad (Suggested: 99% of close taps meet this target).
Ads may not open external browsers, app stores, or other apps unless the user explicitly taps the ad's own call-to-action; automatic redirects to shopping sites are prohibited.
If an ad fails to load, times out, or errors, the user is taken directly to the workout without payment and without being shown the same ad again.

planningFactors.rationale: Finding 3 shows broken ad UX can hijack the app entirely, and finding 1 shows it pushes formerly loyal users away. Scope is medium because it requires ad SDK configuration, close-control handling, and a no-redirect safeguard.

requirements.title: Restore a meaningful free workout path and ad-unlock option
requirements.description: Long-time users say workouts that used to be free are now locked, while reviewers who accept ads note the ad tier is where they live. Balance monetization and retention by guaranteeing a free daily workout and a consistent watch-an-ad unlock path for a rotating set of premium workouts.
acceptanceCriteria: Every user can complete at least one full daily workout without a paid subscription (Suggested: at least one 7-8 minute workout per day, consistent with the praised Daily 7/8 format).

For free-tier users who want more, at least 20 premium workouts per week are unlockable by watching a single ad, and the ad experience follows req-3 requirements (Suggested: at least 20 workouts per week).
Free-tier users see a 'Free workouts remaining today: N' counter on the home screen; when N=0, the app clearly shows both the Subscribe option and the 'watch an ad to unlock' option where available.
At least 10% of the total workout library remains free to all users, and the free selection rotates at least weekly (Suggested: 10% library share and weekly rotation).

planningFactors.rationale: Finding 1 shows the removal of formerly free workouts is the core churn driver; finding 5 shows daily short workouts are the most-loved habit; finding 8 shows some users still find the subscription worth it. This requirement restores the free path without eliminating the paid value proposition.

requirements.title: Honor user goals, restrictions, and no-jump preferences in plans
requirements.description: Users report that onboarding answers and injury avoidances are ignored, plan settings reset unexpectedly, weight-loss goals are forced, and pregnancy or no-jump needs are not respected. Make personalization real: preferences must persist and excluded exercises must never appear in generated plans.
acceptanceCriteria: When a user selects 'avoid knees' or any injury/avoidance, generated plans must not contain exercises tagged with that body part or movement; automated tests must run on at least 100 generated plan variations and return zero prohibited exercises (Suggested: test sample size 100).

Plan settings chosen during onboarding persist for the life of the plan and across app restarts; if the app or an update regenerates a plan, the user receives an explicit notification and can revert to the previous plan.

Onboarding must offer at least these non-weight-loss goals: general fitness, strength, flexibility, and stress relief; users who choose a non-weight-loss goal must not see weight-loss-focused prompts or calorie-loss claims in the generated plan.
A 'no jumping' preference is available in plan settings and, when enabled, removes all exercises tagged 'jump' from the current and future plans.
Pregnancy-safe workout programs must exclude all exercises tagged 'prone' or 'stomach-lying', and each session must show a 'consult your healthcare provider before starting' notice.

planningFactors.rationale: Finding 6 documents ignored preferences and exclusionary content, which damages trust and can pose safety risks. Finding 4 shows content quality is polarizing, so plan generation must at least respect the user's stated constraints. Scope is large because it requires tagging, plan generation logic, and onboarding changes.

requirements.title: Resolve the content-quality split: real-person guidance, consistent cues, fresh routines
requirements.description: Some reviewers praise the variety, demos, and results; others call the newer content 'AI slop', say the voice and visual are mismatched, or report repetitive daily plans. Keep the loved variety while removing the quality issues by auditing high-usage demos, making new content consistent, and balancing muscle-group rotation.
acceptanceCriteria: Audit a sample of the 200 most-used workouts (Suggested sample: top 200 by usage) and re-render or replace any demo where the voice instruction conflicts with the visual movement; the target is no more than 1% of audited demos with a flagged mismatch (Suggested: target 0 mismatches).

New workout content must use real-person video or a consistently animated 3D character with anatomically correct joint motion; static AI-style illustrations should not be the primary demo format for new releases.

Daily and generated workout plans must not repeat the same muscle group more than two consecutive days (derived from the reviewer complaint of legs every day for 10 days; Suggested: max 2 consecutive days per muscle group).

At least 50% of new workout releases should be short format (under 15 minutes) to preserve the praised short-workout strength, while continuing to offer 20-60 minute options (Suggested: 50% of new releases short format).

planningFactors.rationale: Finding 4 shows the same workout library is beloved by some and criticized by others; finding 7 and finding 5 provide concrete directions for demos and short sessions. Scope is large because it involves content production, demo assets, and plan-generation rotation rules.

requirements.title: Add Apple Watch integration for calorie tracking and workout progress sync
requirements.description: Reviewers explicitly ask for Apple Watch/HealthKit sync so calories burned are counted automatically instead of manually, and one reviewer notes progress tracking is lost across devices. Add Apple Watch integration to close this concrete opportunity.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can connect Apple Watch via HealthKit in Settings > Integrations; connection is completed in no more than 5 steps and without leaving the app (Suggested: 5 steps or fewer).
Completed workouts automatically log calories to Apple Health, and the calorie value shown in the app matches Health's active calories within 10% (Suggested: within 10%).
User streak, workout history, and favorites sync between iPhone and Apple Watch within 60 seconds (Suggested: within 60 seconds).

planningFactors.rationale: Finding 7 contains the direct Apple Watch request, and finding 4 shows a reviewer wishing the app connected to a watch. Scope is medium because HealthKit integration and watch app work are moderate.

requirements.title: Ship adaptive and inclusive workout programs for underserved needs
requirements.description: Users ask for programs for older adults with stiff joints, no-floor options, and pregnancy-safe workouts that do not include stomach-lying moves. Add dedicated programs and filters so the app serves bodies of all ages and conditions.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a 'No-Floor' program and an 'Older Adult / Stiff Joints' program, each with at least 10 workouts (Suggested: 14-day programs).
Add a 'Pregnancy-Safe' program filter; selecting it removes all exercises tagged 'prone' or 'stomach-lying' and shows a 'consult your healthcare provider before starting' notice.
The workout library supports filters for no jumping, no floor, chair-friendly, and pregnancy-safe; each filter can be combined with duration and body-focus filters.

planningFactors.rationale: Finding 6 documents the pregnancy-safety complaint and forced-goal problem; finding 7 contains the older-adult program request; finding 4 shows no-floor workouts are already appreciated. Scope is medium because it adds new content and filtering logic.

requirements.title: Add workout control options: halfway/countdown voice prompts, interval length, jump toggle
requirements.description: Reviewers request verbal prompts for halfway and end-of-move countdowns, longer interval time, and a way to turn off jumping. Deliver optional workout controls that make sessions feel more guided and accessible.
acceptanceCriteria: Optional voice prompts are available in settings; when enabled, every workout of 7+ minutes announces 'halfway' at the midpoint and a 3-second '3, 2, 1' countdown at the end of each move (Suggested: 3-second countdown).

Advanced interval settings let users set work/rest duration from 10 to 60 seconds in 5-second increments, and the selection persists for all subsequent workouts (Suggested: 10-60 seconds in 5-second increments).
A 'no jumping' toggle and a 'no floor' toggle in settings modify the current plan and show a 'Plan modified' indicator.
When a workout contains floor exercises and no-floor is enabled, the app substitutes a standing alternative in at least the top 50 most-used workouts (Suggested: top 50 by usage).

planningFactors.rationale: Finding 7 includes the voice-prompt and shorter-ad requests; finding 6 includes the no-jump and longer-interval requests; finding 5 shows the daily short workout is a loved habit that these controls protect. Scope is medium because it touches settings, workout player, and plan substitution.

requirements.title: Rebuild subscription value messaging around outcomes, flexibility, and fairness
requirements.description: Subscription value is deeply polarized: some reviewers call it life-changing and cheaper than a gym, while others call the same price an unjustified paywall, often because of billing surprises. Make pricing transparent, offer real plan flexibility, and reinforce value with outcome-based messaging.
acceptanceCriteria: All paywall and subscription marketing copy states the exact monthly and annual price, what is included, and renewal terms before purchase; no annual plan may be pre-selected over monthly.

A 'Why Premium?' screen is shown once before subscribing and lists concrete included benefits such as unlimited workouts, no ads, offline access, and new content, plus a line comparing the monthly price to a typical gym membership where that claim is true (Suggested: only show the comparison if the claim can be factually supported).
After 30 days of subscription, the app presents each user a 'Your results' summary showing workouts completed, streak, and calories burned (Suggested: show at 30 days).
Users who attempt to cancel are shown a one-screen value summary with both 'Continue Premium' and 'Cancel' options; canceling never requires contacting support.

planningFactors.rationale: Finding 8 explicitly shows the same subscription is seen as transformative by some and as a paywall by others; finding 1 shows former free access is the main complaint; finding 2 shows billing surprises amplify the negative view. This requirement directly addresses the polarizing value perception and depends on transparent labeling first.

requirements.title: Deliver responsive support and account recovery for billing and login issues
requirements.description: Reviewers report support emails being blocked as spam, no reply after multiple messages, and no way to recover a paid account or get a refund. Make support reachable, responsive, and capable of restoring accounts.
acceptanceCriteria: The support contact form accepts every valid submission without spam-blocking legitimate user messages, and each submission returns an automatic ticket ID.

First response to non-billing support requests is within 2 business days; billing disputes get a first response within 1 business day (Suggested: 2 business days for general, 1 business day for billing).

Users who cannot log in can start an account recovery flow by email; if the email is not found, support can verify identity using an App Store receipt and restore account access within 3 business days (Suggested: 3 business days).
All billing/subscription support tickets have a resolved status or a clear next-step response within 5 business days (Suggested: 5 business days).

planningFactors.rationale: Finding 2 shows support failures compound billing and login issues, turning a bad moment into a permanent trust loss. Implementable independently as a support workflow and form fix, so it belongs in the trust-focused first version.

versions.name: 1.0 Trust & Monetization Fixes
versions.summary: Fix the highest-severity problems: make paywall boundaries explicit, guarantee free-trial and billing integrity, repair the free-tier ad experience, preserve a meaningful free workout path, and make support responsive.
versions.rationale: Findings 1, 2, 3, 5, and 8 show that surprise charges, unlabeled paywalls, forced 90-second ads, and unreachable support are the most severe and trust-damaging themes. These issues also drive the polarizing subscription-value split, so they must be addressed before content or personalization work can land effectively.

versions.name: 2.0 Content, Personalization & Opportunities
versions.summary: Resolve the polarizing workout-content split, honor user goals and restrictions, and ship concrete requests: Apple Watch sync, adaptive programs, and workout control options. Rebuild subscription value messaging around outcomes and flexibility.
versions.rationale: Findings 4, 6, and 7 show that after trust issues are fixed, the next lever is making the app feel tailored, safe, and genuinely useful. These changes directly address the 'AI slop' vs 'love the variety' split and the unmet needs expressed by older, pregnant, or injury-avoiding users.

assumptions.text: Our monetization system uses StoreKit 2 or equivalent, which supports transparent in-app subscription management, renewal reminders, and refund status queries.
assumptions.basis: Several findings describe App Store purchases and cancellations; fixing them requires store-level integration but no new backend billing system.

assumptions.text: The team has the ability to generate real-person or high-quality 3D demo content for new workouts and can re-render or remove existing 'AI slop' illustrations.
assumptions.basis: Reviewers request real-person demos and criticize AI-style visuals, but the reviews do not confirm the current content production pipeline.

assumptions.text: Keeping at least one free daily workout and a rotating set of ad-unlockable workouts will not destroy subscription conversion and is the best balance of the polarizing feedback.
assumptions.basis: Reviewers both praise the free daily short workout and complain that formerly free content is locked; the exact conversion impact cannot be measured from review text alone.

assumptions.text: Support response-time targets, ad close-control targets, and other proposed numeric thresholds are operational goals, not currently measured or guaranteed metrics.
assumptions.basis: These thresholds are based on reviewer-reported pain but there is no telemetry in the review data to confirm current baseline performance.

items.label: Subscription value: praise, complaints, and perceived worth
Workout usability: ease, friction, and feature-specific reactions
Most impactful problems: frequent or strongly negative themes
Opportunities: unmet needs, requests, and positive potential
Polarizing features: same feature loved by some, disliked by others
